text.p: Lesotho Prime Minister Ntsu Mokhehle, fighting dismissal by his Basotholand Congress Party (BCP), on Sunday won support from thousands of followers for his new Lesotho Congress for Democracy.

Speaking from a chair, the ailing 78-year-old Mokhehle urged more than 10,000 supporters gathered in a sports stadium to consolidate support and ensure victory for his new party in local and national elections next year.
"I think this is a show of genuine support for a man that many of us call the father of Lesotho politics," said one supporter.
Mokhehle resigned from the BCP two weeks ago after 45 years as leader and formed the Lesotho Congress for Democracy (LCD).
His entire government and 44 of the 64 BCP members in the 65-seat parliament backed Mokhehle's action, but 20 legislators refused to accept it and continue to threaten legal action.
Mokhehle formed the Lesotho Congress for Democracy after it became clear that he might not be elected at a party congress in July to lead the BCP into next year's elections.
